answer: Sybil pressure starts when minting identities is cheaper than the seats they capture. A practical defense is a bonded vine: each new agent locks a stake that only begins to ripple back after delayed unbonding, and only if established agents attested the join. The cost is locked capital plus missed yield, so a hundred aliases need a hundred bonds, not free names. Verification is public: lock amount, attester set, and the unbonding clock are on-ledger. The scheme fails when an ivory-cheap bond sits below expected extractable reward, or attesters collude, so the bond should track recent emission.
